findings.title: Commits at Tasks 6, 7 and 9 would land with failing tests; their tests come 3–4 tasks later
findings.description:
- **Task 6** removes the `is_rate_limit_event(exc.data)` special case (`src/squadron/providers/sdk/agent.py:128`). After that, `test_a_rejected_rate_limit_event_reaches_the_backoff` (`tests/providers/sdk/test_agent.py:648`) fails. It feeds in a `MessageParseError` with a `rate_limit_event` payload, which is now skipped with a WARNING instead of backing off.
- **Task 9** deletes `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`. The four `test_the_shim_*` tests import it locally (`test_agent.py:701-760`), so they fail at that commit.
- **Task 7** removes the shim from `sdk_session.py`, but the exclusion-set fix is in Task 8. Until then, informational events reach `response_parts` (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:173`). That brings back the issue #23 leak in Task 7's commit.

The rewrites that make these green are in Task 10 (after 6 and 9) and Task 11 (after 7). This breaks the test-with pattern. A junior AI running tests at Task 6 will see red with no instruction on what to do.

**Fix:**
- Put each test rewrite directly after its implementation: Task 10's agent.py rewrites after Task 6, Task 11 after Task 7.
- Delete the four shim tests in the same task that deletes the shim.
- Merge Task 8 into Task 7.

findings.title: Task 6 contradicts itself on informational events
findings.description:
The step says: "log at DEBUG and continue the loop **without yielding it** to the caller … **let it flow to translation** as normal." Both can't be true. In query and client mode, `translate_sdk_message` runs in the caller on whatever `_skip_unparseable` yields (`agent.py:155-156`, `agent.py:203-205`). If the event isn't yielded, translation never sees it.

The slice has the same tension: D4 says informational events "must not reach translation", while D6 says they should be "observable rather than dropped". The task should pick one and say so. Two options:
- Yield informational events so Task 4's translation branch is reachable in agent mode.
- Skip them in `_skip_unparseable`, and accept that D6's branch only matters for pipeline `dispatch`.

Whichever is chosen, Task 10's `allowed_warning` test needs to assert the matching behavior (message yielded or not).

findings.title: Task 6 misses the third `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER` check, which risks Success Criterion 6
findings.description:
Task 6 says to replace "both `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER in str(exc)` gates". Query mode has a second check at line 180 that decides whether running out of retries raises `ProviderRateLimitError` or a plain `ProviderError`.

Task 2 never says what message `RateLimitRejected` carries. If the message doesn't contain `"rate_limit"`, a run that exhausts retries on typed events raises a plain `ProviderError`. That violates SC6. `test_exhausted_rate_limit_raises_a_distinct_error` would catch it, but only in Task 10, and only if the implementer reads the failure correctly.

**Fix:** have Task 6 also replace line 180 with `_is_throttle(exc)`. Alternatively, have Task 2 require that `RateLimitRejected`'s message contains `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER`.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes and appear after every task
findings.description:
Every task ends with `- [ ] Commit: ...`. That's 14 commit checkboxes. Commit markers should be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checkboxes, placed at working, tested points rather than after every task.

The file is also heavier than a slice with effort 3/5 needs, at 16 tasks:
- Task 8 is a one-line change in the same loop as Task 7.
- Task 12 is verify-only and duplicates Task 13's `pytest tests/providers tests/metrology` run.
- Tasks 3 and 5 could be folded into Tasks 2 and 4 under test-with.

**Fix:** merge 8→7, 12→13, 3→2 and 5→4. Use roughly 4–5 plain `**Commit**:` markers:
1. After the dependency bump.
2. After classification and translation with their tests.
3. After agent.py with its tests.
4. After sdk_session with its tests and the shim deletion.
5. After closeout.

findings.title: Success Criterion 7 ends up with only a unit test
findings.description: Task 10 converts every plain `ClaudeSDKError("rate_limit...")` test to a typed event. After that, the retained substring path (genuine 429) is covered only by Task 3's direct `_is_throttle` unit test. That's adequate because all three gates call `_is_throttle`. Still, keeping one existing retry test aimed at a plain 429-style message (one that doesn't match Task 10's grep) would preserve end-to-end proof of SC7 at almost no cost.

findings.title: Client-mode docstring will be stale and no task covers it
findings.description: `_handle_client_mode`'s docstring says "when the CLI emits a `rate_limit_event` the SDK raises `ClaudeSDKError`". After the upgrade that's false. Part B asks for stale docstrings and comments to be rewritten, but Task 6 only rewrites `_skip_unparseable`'s docstring. Add a sub-item to Task 6.

findings.title: Shim grep only checks `src/`, while SC2 covers `src/` and `tests/`
findings.description: Task 9's success grep only checks `src`. Task 10 deletes the tests that reference the shim, so the outcome is right, but no step verifies `grep -rn install_rate_limit_parser_shim tests` as walkthrough step 1 does. Add it to Task 10's or Task 13's success line.

findings.title: No unit test asserts the WARNING required by SC3
findings.description: SC3 requires a WARNING that names the attempt number. Only Task 15's manual forced-throttle check confirms it. That meets the walkthrough. A `caplog` assertion in one of Task 10's rewritten tests would make it a regression test, but this is optional.
